statement: For a negative involution in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group, its centre-free extension has one F-conjugacy class of order-two sections with fixed-subgroup H1(-,F2)=0 when its homology action modulo two is nonidentity, and two classes with fixed-subgroup H1 dimensions one and zero when that action is identity. The normalizer of each section is exactly C_F(S) times S. The full cusp normalizer is dihedral, and its two internal reflection classes fuse under F-conjugacy in the full extension. For every cusp reflection v there is an actual g in F with g v g^-1=c v and c=[g,v].
depends_on: D27 actual involution lift; D43 global involution multiplier; A7 exact cusp normalizer in F; Hochschild-Serre and explicit coefficient Bocksteins; Kochloukova-Zalesskii full-profinite Brown restriction theorem, Theorem 2 and Section 1.1
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The integral plus/minus decomposition is an explicit idempotent decomposition of the actual cohomology module. No change of the free profinite generating pair is inferred. The full Brown restriction map and its cohomological-dimension hypotheses are stated explicitly.
notes: In the identity-modulo-two case, the coefficient Bockstein gives a^2=0 and b^2=u b. Associativity forces a b=epsilon u a. The localized degree-zero cohomology algebra is explicitly isomorphic to the dual numbers over F2 times F2. Brown restriction identifies its two local factors with the two section normalizers and yields the exact fixed-subgroup cohomology dimensions. In the nonidentity-modulo-two case the regular F2[C2]-module makes high cohomology one-dimensional and gives one section class. The two cusp reflections have identical abelian characters, and the two full classes, when present, are distinguished by the b character, so cusp fusion follows in the full group. No full triviality or procyclicity of a fixed subgroup is asserted from its H1 dimension. The finite certificate checks exact cochains, finite algebra isomorphisms and free-word examples; it does not substitute finite quotients for the full restriction theorem.
